tool_response:
1: """Estimating obstacle velocity from the robot's own LiDAR.
   2: 
   3: This is the half of ``dwa_predictive`` that makes it a candidate rather
   4: than a thought experiment. P4's oracle proved the constant-velocity model
   5: is worth something *given perfect perception*; this module has to earn
   6: some of that back from two consecutive scans, and **the estimation error
   7: it carries is part of the algorithm, not something it is excused from**.
   8: 
   9: **Why it may not simply read the answer.** ``dwa`` declares
  10: ``local_observation_class = "lidar_only"``. A predictive controller that
  11: took velocities from ``engine.dynamic_obstacles_now()`` would become a
  12: ``lidar+human_states`` candidate, and the platform's ranking refuses to
  13: compare across observation classes by default â€” because a candidate that
  14: knows where everything is will beat one that has to look, and that
  15: victory says nothing about prediction. So the velocities are estimated
  16: here, from ``Observation`` alone, and the estimator's failures are the
  17: candidate's failures.
  18: 
  19: The pipeline, and the classification step is the one people skip::
  20: 
  21:     scan  ->  [1] cluster        adjacent rays, split on a range jump
  22:               [2] classify       wall / edge-clipped / free-standing
  23:               [3] associate      nearest centroid inside a gate
  24:               [4] estimate       least squares over a few frames
  25:               [5] floor          below which "moving" is just noise
  26:               [6] lifecycle      warm-up, loss, ambiguity
  27: 
  28: **Every failure mode falls back to ``dwa``.** A broken tracker must make
  29: this controller behave like the one without prediction, never like one
  30: carrying rubbish velocities. That is why each stage below answers
  31: uncertainty with **zero velocity** rather than a guess: a track with no
  32: velocity contributes nothing to the predictive cost, which is exactly
  33: ``dwa``.
  34: 
  35: **Thresholds come from the sensor, never from the scenario.** An earlier
  36: draft sized the cluster split from the largest ``DynamicObstacle.radius``
  37: the deployment declared. That is ground truth: a ``lidar_only`` candidate
  38: reading it knows *how big the things in this room are* before it has seen
  39: them, and the leak surfaces the moment somebody runs it on an unfamiliar
  40: map. The split is derived from ray spacing and declared range noise
  41: instead â€” the controller's own specification, which it is entitled to.
  42: """
  43: 
  44: from __future__ import annotations
  45: 
  46: import math
  47: from dataclasses import dataclass, field
  48: 
  49: from planbench_planning.dwa_predictive.tracks import ObstacleTrack
  50: from planbench_schemas.episode import Observation
  51: from planbench_schemas.feasibility import SafetyEnvelope
  52: from planbench_schemas.geometry import EPS, Point2D
  53: from planbench_schemas.sensor import SensorNoise
  54: 
  55: __all__ = ["Cluster", "LidarTracker", "TrackerDiagnostics"]
  56: 
  57: 
  58: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  59: class Cluster:
  60:     """A run of adjacent rays that plausibly hit one object."""
  61: 
  62:     centroid: Point2D
  63:     width: float
  64:     points: int
  65:     #: Straight-line residual of the points, in metres. Small on a wall.
  66:     straightness: float
  67:     #: True when the run ends because the scan ran out rather than because
  68:     #: the object did â€” its far side is unknown, so its centre is not a
  69:     #: quantity that can be tracked.
  70:     clipped: bool
  71: 
  72:     @property
  73:     def radius(self) -> float:
  74:         """Half the width, floored so a one-ray return is not zero-sized."""
  75:         return max(self.width / 2.0, 0.05)
  76: 
  77: 
  78: @dataclass
  79: class TrackerDiagnostics:
  80:     """Counters for reading a run afterwards, never for scoring one.
  81: 
  82:     Deliberately not metrics. The Metrics Engine reads the trace and the
  83:     gates read the metrics; a number produced here would be a second
  84:     source for the same question (HÄ-5). These exist so that when a
  85:     comparison comes out flat somebody can ask *did the tracker even
  86:     work* without re-running anything.
  87:     """
  88: 
  89:     frames: int = 0
  90:     clusters_seen: int = 0
  91:     clusters_tracked: int = 0
  92:     associations: int = 0
  93:     ambiguous_drops: int = 0
  94:     tracks_started: int = 0
  95:     tracks_timed_out: int = 0
  96:     floored: int = 0
  97:     #: Frames a track was alive but unobserved, and therefore silent.
  98:     coasting: int = 0
  99: 
 100:     def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, int]:
 101:         return {
 102:             "frames": self.frames,
 103:             "clusters_seen": self.clusters_seen,
 104:             "clusters_tracked": self.clusters_tracked,
 105:             "associations": self.associations,
 106:             "ambiguous_drops": self.ambiguous_drops,
 107:             "tracks_started": self.tracks_started,
 108:             "tracks_timed_out": self.tracks_timed_out,
 109:             "floored": self.floored,
 110:             "coasting": self.coasting,
 111:         }
 112: 
 113: 
 114: @dataclass
 115: class _Track:
 116:     """One followed object and the short history its velocity comes from."""
 117: 
 118:     identity: int
 119:     #: ``(time, x, y)`` newest last, capped at the estimation window.
 120:     history: list[tuple[float, float, float]] = field(default_factory=list)
 121:     radius: float = 0.2
 122:     last_seen: float = 0.0
 123:     misses: int = 0
 124: 
 125:     @property
 126:     def center(self) -> Point2D:
 127:         _, x, y = self.history[-1]
 128:         return Point2D(x=x, y=y)
 129: 
 130: 
 131: class LidarTracker:
 132:     """Clusters a scan, follows the free-standing parts, estimates velocity.
 133: 
 134:     Holds state between control steps â€” the first thing in this
 135:     controller that does â€” so :meth:`reset` has to clear **all** of it.
 136:     Two episodes on one instance must equal two instances, and that is a
 137:     test rather than an intention.
 138:     """
 139: 
 140:     def __init__(
 141:         self,
 142:         config,
 143:         envelope: SafetyEnvelope | None = None,
 144:         sensor_noise: SensorNoise | None = None,
 145:     ) -> None:
 146:         self._config = config
 147:         self._envelope = envelope or SafetyEnvelope()
 148:         self._noise = sensor_noise or SensorNoise()
 149:         self._tracks: list[_Track] = []
 150:         self._next_identity = 0
 151:         self.diagnostics = TrackerDiagnostics()
 152: 
 153:     def reset(self) -> None:
 154:         self._tracks = []
 155:         self._next_identity = 0
 156:         self.diagnostics = TrackerDiagnostics()
 157: 
 158:     # -- the pipeline ---------------------------------------------------
 159: 
 160:     def update(self, observation: Observation) -> tuple[ObstacleTrack, ...]:
 161:         """One scan in, the tracks it supports out."""
 162:         self.diagnostics.frames += 1
 163: 
 164:         clusters = self.cluster(observation)
 165:         self.diagnostics.clusters_seen += len(clusters)
 166:         movable = [c for c in clusters if self._is_free_standing(c)]
 167:         self.diagnostics.clusters_tracked += len(movable)
 168: 
 169:         self._associate(movable, observation.time)
 170:         self._expire(observation.time)
 171: 
 172:         here = Point2D(x=observation.pose.x, y=observation.pose.y)
 173:         spacing = 2.0 * math.pi / max(len(observation.lidar_ranges), 1)
 174:         out: list[ObstacleTrack] = []
 175:         for track in self._tracks:
 176:             reach = math.hypot(track.center.x - here.x, track.center.y - here.y)
 177:             floor = self.velocity_floor(reach, spacing)
 178:             velocity, confidence = self._velocity_of(track, floor)
 179:             out.append(
 180:                 ObstacleTrack(
 181:                     center=track.center,
 182:                     radius=track.radius,
 183:                     velocity=velocity,
 184:                     confidence=confidence,
 185:                 )
 186:             )
 187:         # Sorted by identity so the order a controller sees is a function
 188:         # of when things were first seen, not of list churn. Determinism
 189:         # is a contract here, not a nicety.
 190:         return tuple(out)
 191: 
 192:     def cluster(self, observation: Observation) -> tuple[Cluster, ...]:
 193:         """Split the scan into runs of adjacent rays on one surface.
 194: 
 195:         Two neighbouring rays that hit the same flat surface at range
 196:         ``r`` land about ``r Â· Î”Î¸`` apart, so a gap much larger than that
 197:         means the surface ended. The threshold is that quantity times a
 198:         declared factor, plus a margin for the declared range noise â€” both
 199:         from the sensor's own specification.
 200: 
 201:         Rays that returned nothing are not obstacles at maximum range;
 202:         they are the absence of an obstacle, and they end a run.
 203:         """
 204:         ranges = observation.lidar_ranges
 205:         if not ranges:
 206:             return ()
 207:         config = self._config
 208:         rays = len(ranges)
 209:         spacing = 2.0 * math.pi / rays
 210:         start_angle = observation.pose.theta - math.pi
 211:         limit = max(ranges)
 212: 
 213:         runs: list[list[int]] = []
 214:         current: list[int] = []
 215:         for index, distance in enumerate(ranges):
 216:             if distance >= limit - EPS:
 217:                 if current:
 218:                     runs.append(current)
 219:                     current = []
 220:                 continue
 221:             if current:
 222:                 previous = ranges[current[-1]]
 223:                 threshold = (
 224:                     config.cluster_gap_factor * distance * spacing
 225:                     + config.cluster_range_margin * max(self._noise.lidar_range_sigma_m, 1e-6)
 226:                 )
 227:                 if abs(distance - previous) > threshold or index != current[-1] + 1:
 228:                     runs.append(current)
 229:                     current = []
 230:             current.append(index)
 231:         if current:
 232:             runs.append(current)
 233: 
 234:         # The scan wraps: a run touching ray 0 and one touching the last
 235:         # ray are one object seen across the seam. Joining them is what
 236:         # stops an obstacle directly behind the robot being read as two.
 237:         if len(runs) > 1 and runs[0][0] == 0 and runs[-1][-1] == rays - 1:
 238:             runs[0] = runs[-1] + runs[0]
 239:             runs.pop()
 240: 
 241:         clusters = []
 242:         for run in runs:
 243:             points = [
 244:                 (
 245:                     observation.pose.x + ranges[i] * math.cos(start_angle + i * spacing),
 246:                     observation.pose.y + ranges[i] * math.sin(start_angle + i * spacing),
 247:                 )
 248:                 for i in run
 249:             ]
 250:             clusters.append(self._describe(points, run, rays, ranges, limit))
 251:         return tuple(clusters)
 252: 
 253:     def _describe(self, points, run, rays, ranges, limit) -> Cluster:
 254:         count = len(points)
 255:         cx = sum(p[0] for p in points) / count
 256:         cy = sum(p[1] for p in points) / count
 257:         first, last = points[0], points[-1]
 258:         width = math.hypot(last[0] - first[0], last[1] - first[1])
 259: 
 260:         # Residual of the points about the chord: near zero on a flat
 261:         # surface, larger on something curved like a person or a cart.
 262:         straightness = 0.0
 263:         if count > 2 and width > EPS:
 264:             dx, dy = (last[0] - first[0]) / width, (last[1] - first[1]) / width
 265:             for x, y in points:
 266:                 straightness = max(straightness, abs((x - first[0]) * dy - (y - first[1]) * dx))
 267: 
 268:         # **Bounded on both sides by free space is the good case**, and
 269:         # getting this polarity backwards silently disables the tracker:
 270:         # an isolated object in an open room is *always* flanked by rays
 271:         # that returned nothing, so reading "no return beside it" as
 272:         # clipped rejects exactly the objects worth following.
 273:         #
 274:         # A run is clipped when a neighbouring ray **did** return
 275:         # something that the gap threshold split off â€” the surface carries
 276:         # on past the break, so this run is a slice of a larger structure
 277:         # and its centroid is a property of where the split fell rather
 278:         # than of any object.
 279:         before = ranges[(run[0] - 1) % rays]
 280:         after = ranges[(run[-1] + 1) % rays]
 281:         clipped = before < limit - EPS or after < limit - EPS
 282:         return Cluster(
 283:             centroid=Point2D(x=cx, y=cy),
 284:             width=width,
 285:             points=count,
 286:             straightness=straightness,
 287:             clipped=clipped,
 288:         )
 289: 
 290:     def _is_free_standing(self, cluster: Cluster) -> bool:
 291:         """Whether this cluster has a centre worth following.
 292: 
 293:         **Not a size test.** Sizing the decision from the obstacles the
 294:         scenario declares would be reading ground truth. The three signals
 295:         below are all properties of the scan itself:
 296: 
 297:         * **clipped** â€” the run ended because the scan did, so the far
 298:           side is unknown and the centroid moves when the *view* changes
 299:           rather than when the object does;
 300:         * **long and straight** â€” a wall or a shelf face. It has a
 301:           centroid, and that centroid slides along the wall as the robot
 302:           drives past, which is a velocity that does not exist;
 303:         * **too few points** â€” one or two returns give a centroid
 304:           dominated by range noise.
 305:         """
 306:         config = self._config
 307:         if cluster.clipped:
 308:             return False
 309:         if cluster.points < config.cluster_min_points:
 310:             return False
 311:         if cluster.width > config.cluster_max_width:
 312:             return False
 313:         return not (
 314:             cluster.width > config.cluster_wall_width
 315:             and cluster.straightness < config.cluster_straightness
 316:         )
 317: 
 318:     def _associate(self, clusters: list[Cluster], time: float) -> None:
 319:         """Match clusters to existing tracks, nearest centroid in a gate.
 320: 
 321:         The gate is ``association_speed_limit Â· Î”t`` plus a margin, and
 322:         that limit is **candidate-owned** â€” deliberately not
 323:         ``v_obstacle_max``. The two fail in different ways: a wrong
 324:         ``v_obstacle_max`` breaks a braking guarantee and ends in a
 325:         collision, while a wrong association limit only breaks matching,
 326:         and a tracker that stops matching falls back to ``dwa``. Two
 327:         different failure modes may not share one field.
 328:         """
 329:         config = self._config
 330:         unmatched = list(clusters)
 331:         for track in self._tracks:
 332:             elapsed = max(time - track.last_seen, config.control_period)
 333:             gate = config.association_speed_limit * elapsed + config.association_margin
 334:             inside = [
 335:                 cluster
 336:                 for cluster in unmatched
 337:                 if math.hypot(
 338:                     cluster.centroid.x - track.center.x,
 339:                     cluster.centroid.y - track.center.y,
 340:                 )
 341:                 <= gate
 342:             ]
 343:             if len(inside) > 1:
 344:                 # **Ambiguous, so take neither.** Two objects passing each
 345:                 # other is the case this protects against: matching across
 346:                 # them produces two velocities pointing the wrong way,
 347:                 # which is worse than no velocity at all.
 348:                 self.diagnostics.ambiguous_drops += 1
 349:                 track.misses += 1
 350:                 continue
 351:             if not inside:
 352:                 track.misses += 1
 353:                 continue
 354:             chosen = inside[0]
 355:             unmatched.remove(chosen)
 356:             track.history.append((time, chosen.centroid.x, chosen.centroid.y))
 357:             del track.history[: -config.velocity_window]
 358:             track.radius = chosen.radius
 359:             track.last_seen = time
 360:             track.misses = 0
 361:             self.diagnostics.associations += 1
 362: 
 363:         for cluster in unmatched:
 364:             self._tracks.append(
 365:                 _Track(
 366:                     identity=self._next_identity,
 367:                     history=[(time, cluster.centroid.x, cluster.centroid.y)],
 368:                     radius=cluster.radius,
 369:                     last_seen=time,
 370:                 )
 371:             )
 372:             self._next_identity += 1
 373:             self.diagnostics.tracks_started += 1
 374: 
 375:     def _expire(self, time: float) -> None:
 376:         """Drop tracks nothing has matched for a while.
 377: 
 378:         Kept for a few frames first, because partial occlusion is
 379:         ordinary: deleting on the first miss would restart the estimate
 380:         every time something passed behind a shelf, and the velocity would
 381:         be zero exactly when it mattered. An object that reappears after
 382:         the timeout becomes a **new** track â€” re-identification across a
 383:         long gap is a different problem and not one this MVP claims.
 384:         """
 385:         keep = []
 386:         for track in self._tracks:
 387:             if time - track.last_seen > self._config.track_timeout:
 388:                 self.diagnostics.tracks_timed_out += 1
 389:                 continue
 390:             keep.append(track)
 391:         self._tracks = keep
 392: 
 393:     def velocity_floor(self, reach: float, ray_spacing: float) -> float:
 394:         """Speed below which "moving" is indistinguishable from not moving.
 395: 
 396:         **Derived, not chosen** â€” the same discipline as ``SafetyEnvelope``
 397:         and ``N_min``. Three sources, and the third is the one an earlier
 398:         draft of this module left out:
 399: 
 400:         * **localisation** â€” a robot wrong about its own pose puts that
 401:           error into every world-frame point it computes, so a wall
 402:           acquires a velocity;
 403:         * **range noise** â€” straight into the centroid;
 404:         * **the scan itself.** A cluster is sampled by discrete rays, so
 405:           its centroid moves when the *set of rays hitting it* changes,
 406:           which happens whenever the robot moves. One ray spacing at that
 407:           object's range, ``reach Â· Î”Î¸``, is the scale of that shift, and
 408:           it exists with a **perfect** sensor.
 409: 
 410:         The third term is not theoretical. Measured on three fully static
 411:         scenes with every noise stream **off**, the tracker reported
 412:         phantom speeds with a median of 0.28â€“0.41 m/s and peaks at
 413:         1.27 m/s â€” the same magnitude as the real traffic in this library.
 414:         With only the first two terms the floor is exactly zero there, and
 415:         every one of those phantoms reaches the cost function.
 416: 
 417:         This is the single most important line in the module. Without it
 418:         ``dwa_predictive`` is **worse** than ``dwa`` on every static
 419:         scene, and worse precisely where the deployment declares
 420:         localisation noise â€” which is where the project wants to measure.

1: """Simulated planar LiDAR via grid ray casting (Amanatidesâ€“Woo DDA).
   2: 
   3: Conventions:
   4: - A ray stops at the entry face of the first blocked cell (OCCUPIED, or
   5:   UNKNOWN when the grid treats unknown as occupied) and returns that
   6:   distance, clamped to ``max_range``.
   7: - A ray that leaves the map without hitting a blocked cell returns
   8:   ``max_range`` (the void beyond the map reflects nothing; maps should
   9:   model physical walls explicitly).
  10: - A sensor origin inside a blocked cell returns 0.0 for every ray.
  11: 
  12: Deterministic: no randomness, no noise model (a seeded noise model can
  13: be layered on later without changing this module).
  14: """
  15: 
  16: from __future__ import annotations
  17: 
  18: import math
  19: 
  20: from planbench_schemas.geometry import Pose2D
  21: from planbench_schemas.sensor import LidarConfig
  22: from planbench_simulator.grid import OccupancyGrid
  23: 
  24: 
  25: def cast_ray(grid: OccupancyGrid, x: float, y: float, angle: float, max_range: float) -> float:
  26:     """Distance from (x, y) along ``angle`` to the first blocked cell.
  27: 
  28:     Raises:
  29:         ValueError: If the origin lies outside the map or ``max_range``
  30:             is not a finite positive number.
  31:     """
  32:     if not math.isfinite(max_range) or max_range <= 0:
  33:         raise ValueError(f"max_range must be a finite positive number, got {max_range!r}")
  34:     start_cell = grid.world_to_grid(x, y)
  35:     if start_cell is None:
  36:         raise ValueError(f"ray origin ({x}, {y}) is outside the map")
  37:     row, col = start_cell
  38:     if grid.is_blocked_cell(row, col):
  39:         return 0.0
  40: 
  41:     direction_x = math.cos(angle)
  42:     direction_y = math.sin(angle)
  43:     resolution = grid.resolution
  44:     origin_x, origin_y = grid.origin.x, grid.origin.y
  45: 
  46:     step_col = 1 if direction_x > 0 else -1 if direction_x < 0 else 0
  47:     step_row = 1 if direction_y > 0 else -1 if direction_y < 0 else 0
  48: 
  49:     if direction_x > 0:
  50:         t_max_x = (origin_x + (col + 1) * resolution - x) / direction_x
  51:         t_delta_x = resolution / direction_x
  52:     elif direction_x < 0:
  53:         t_max_x = (origin_x + col * resolution - x) / direction_x
  54:         t_delta_x = resolution / -direction_x
  55:     else:
  56:         t_max_x = math.inf
  57:         t_delta_x = math.inf
  58: 
  59:     if direction_y > 0:
  60:         t_max_y = (origin_y + (row + 1) * resolution - y) / direction_y
  61:         t_delta_y = resolution / direction_y
  62:     elif direction_y < 0:
  63:         t_max_y = (origin_y + row * resolution - y) / direction_y
  64:         t_delta_y = resolution / -direction_y
  65:     else:
  66:         t_max_y = math.inf
  67:         t_delta_y = math.inf
  68: 
  69:     while True:
  70:         if t_max_x <= t_max_y:
  71:             t_hit = t_max_x
  72:             t_max_x += t_delta_x
  73:             col += step_col
  74:         else:
  75:             t_hit = t_max_y
  76:             t_max_y += t_delta_y
  77:             row += step_row
  78:         if t_hit > max_range:
  79:             return max_range
  80:         if not (0 <= row < grid.height and 0 <= col < grid.width):
  81:             return max_range
  82:         if grid.is_blocked_cell(row, col):
  83:             return min(t_hit, max_range)
  84: 
  85: 
  86: def scan(grid: OccupancyGrid, pose: Pose2D, config: LidarConfig) -> tuple[float, ...]:
  87:     """Full LiDAR scan at ``pose``; ray i at relative angle
  88:     ``-span/2 + i * span / num_rays`` from the heading."""
  89:     increment = config.angle_span / config.num_rays
  90:     start = pose.theta - config.angle_span / 2.0
  91:     return tuple(
  92:         cast_ray(grid, pose.x, pose.y, start + i * increment, config.max_range)
  93:         for i in range(config.num_rays)
  94:     )

1: """Canonical hashing for contract identities (HÄ-1.3, HÄ-3.1).
   2: 
   3: Both frozen identities in the contract â€” ``candidate_id`` and
   4: ``episode_context_id`` â€” are ``sha256_short(canonical_json(...))``. They
   5: live in different packages but must agree byte for byte, so the two
   6: primitives sit here rather than being reimplemented on each side: an id
   7: computed two slightly different ways would silently split one candidate,
   8: or one episode, into two.
   9: 
  10: This is deliberately *not* the same as ``planbench_benchmark.spec._canonical``,
  11: which builds a ``repr``-based string for the older fairness checksum.
  12: That one must keep hashing exactly as it always has, or every stored
  13: benchmark report would declare itself incomparable.
  14: """
  15: 
  16: from __future__ import annotations
  17: 
  18: import hashlib
  19: import json
  20: 
  21: 
  22: def canonical_json(payload: object) -> str:
  23:     """Deterministic JSON: sorted keys, no incidental whitespace.
  24: 
  25:     Sorted keys are the point â€” a mapping is unordered as data but ordered
  26:     as text, and an id depending on the order somebody typed the fields
  27:     would not be an id.
  28:     """
  29:     return json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)
  30: 
  31: 
  32: def sha256_short(payload: str, *, length: int) -> str:
  33:     """First ``length`` hex characters of the SHA-256 of ``payload``."""
  34:     if length <= 0:
  35:         raise ValueError(f"length must be positive, got {length}")
  36:     return hashlib.sha256(payload.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:length]

1: """Episode context: the conditions one episode runs under (HÄ-3).
   2: 
   3: An episode context is *what varies between episodes* with the candidate
   4: held out of it: which deployment, which mission, which environment
   5: variant, which seed. It exists so a comparison can be paired.
   6: 
   7: > Every candidate in one comparison must run on exactly the same set of
   8: > ``episode_context_id``.
   9: 
  10: That rule is the reason paired bootstrap works at all (HÄ-11.2): because
  11: the candidates faced identical conditions, most of the variance is shared
  12: and cancels in the difference. Break the rule and the difference is
  13: measuring the conditions, not the candidates â€” so the Decision Engine
  14: refuses to compute Î”U rather than computing a wrong one (see
  15: :mod:`planbench_decision.pairing`).
  16: 
  17: **The seed is the whole source of randomness.** Everything stochastic in
  18: an episode â€” dynamic-obstacle placement and trajectories, and any sensor
  19: or odometry noise added later â€” must derive from
  20: :attr:`EpisodeContext.seed`, never from process-global randomness. Today
  21: this holds by construction: the only randomised components are
  22: ``position_at`` (seeded from ``Scenario.random_seed``) and
  23: ``RRTStarPlanner`` (seeded from its config plus the episode seed). No
  24: module in the simulator or planners draws from ``random`` or an unseeded
  25: ``np.random``, so replaying a context id reproduces the episode.
  26: 
  27: This is one of the three identities frozen after week 1 (CONTRACTS Â§0):
  28: trace files, paired statistics and manifests all key on it.
  29: """
  30: 
  31: from __future__ import annotations
  32: 
  33: from typing import Literal
  34: 
  35: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, computed_field, model_validator
  36: 
  37: from planbench_schemas.identity import canonical_json, sha256_short
  38: 
  39: #: Length of the hex digest kept as an id (HÄ-3.1).
  40: EPISODE_CONTEXT_ID_LENGTH = 12
  41: 
  42: #: Which of the two sample sets an episode belongs to (HÄ-3.3).
  43: #:
  44: #: - ``evaluation``: independent draws over mission Ã— obstacle realisation
  45: #:   Ã— seed. The *only* set that may estimate success rate, the collision
  46: #:   upper bound and any performance distribution.
  47: #: - ``neighborhood``: structured perturbations around the nominal
  48: #:   profile. Measures whether the *recommendation* holds up, nothing
  49: #:   else. Runs within one variant are correlated, so pooling them into a
  50: #:   rule-of-three bound would make ``3/N`` far too optimistic (HÄ-11.4).
  51: SampleSet = Literal["evaluation", "neighborhood"]
  52: 
  53: #: The unperturbed environment. Evaluation episodes always run here.
  54: NOMINAL_VARIANT = "nominal"
  55: 
  56: 
  57: class EpisodeContext(BaseModel):
  58:     """One set of episode conditions, identified by its hash (HÄ-3.1).
  59: 
  60:     ``sample_set`` is *not* part of the hash: HÄ-3.1 fixes the hashed
  61:     payload as task profile, mission, environment variant and seed, and an
  62:     id computed from anything else would not match one computed by
  63:     another implementation of the same contract. The set stays reachable
  64:     as a field â€” HÄ-5 records it in trace metadata â€” and it cannot
  65:     disagree with the variant, because the two are constrained to move
  66:     together (see :meth:`_validate_sample_set`).
  67:     """
  68: 
  69:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  70: 
  71:     task_profile_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
  72:     mission_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
  73:     seed: int = Field(ge=0)
  74:     environment_variant: str = Field(default=NOMINAL_VARIANT, min_length=1)
  75:     sample_set: SampleSet = "evaluation"
  76: 
  77:     @model_validator(mode="before")
  78:     @classmethod
  79:     def _drop_declared_identity(cls, value: object) -> object:
  80:         """Accept and discard a serialised id so dumps reload unchanged."""
  81:         if isinstance(value, dict) and "episode_context_id" in value:
  82:             return {k: v for k, v in value.items() if k != "episode_context_id"}
  83:         return value
  84: 
  85:     @model_validator(mode="after")
  86:     def _validate_sample_set(self) -> EpisodeContext:
  87:         """Evaluation runs on the nominal environment, and only there.
  88: 
  89:         Without this the two sets could collide: a neighborhood context
  90:         whose variant was left at ``nominal`` would hash identically to
  91:         the evaluation context for the same mission and seed, and the ban
  92:         on pooling them (HÄ-11.4) would become unenforceable â€” the ids
  93:         alone could no longer tell you which set a row came from.
  94:         """
  95:         nominal = self.environment_variant == NOMINAL_VARIANT
  96:         if self.sample_set == "evaluation" and not nominal:
  97:             raise ValueError(
  98:                 f"evaluation episodes run on the nominal environment, got variant "
  99:                 f"{self.environment_variant!r}; label this context sample_set='neighborhood'"
 100:             )
 101:         if self.sample_set == "neighborhood" and nominal:
 102:             raise ValueError(
 103:                 "a neighborhood episode must name the variant it perturbs; "
 104:                 f"{NOMINAL_VARIANT!r} is the unperturbed environment"
 105:             )
 106:         return self
 107: 
 108:     @computed_field  # type: ignore[prop-decorator]
 109:     @property
 110:     def episode_context_id(self) -> str:
 111:         """Hash of the conditions, exactly as HÄ-3.1 defines the payload."""
 112:         return sha256_short(
 113:             canonical_json(
 114:                 {
 115:                     "task_profile_id": self.task_profile_id,
 116:                     "mission_id": self.mission_id,
 117:                     "environment_variant": self.environment_variant,
 118:                     "seed": self.seed,
 119:                 }
 120:             ),
 121:             length=EPISODE_CONTEXT_ID_LENGTH,
 122:         )

   1: """DWA that rolls the world forward alongside the robot.
   2: 
   3: The whole idea is one missing axis. ``DWAPlanner`` forward-simulates its
   4: own trajectory across the horizon and compares it against **a photograph
   5: of the world at t=0**, held still for the entire rollout::
   6: 
   7:     diff = points[:, :, None, :] - obstacles[None, None, :, :]
   8:     #      (N, K, 2)                (1,  1,  M, 2)   <- no time axis
   9: 
  10: The consequence runs in both directions, and the second is the one people
  11: miss. Against an obstacle that is **leaving**, the controller is too shy:
  12: somebody who has already walked out of the doorway is still standing in
  13: it as far as the rollout is concerned, so the gap scores narrow and the
  14: robot waits for a space that is already empty. Against an obstacle that
  15: is **arriving**, it is too bold: a cart closing at 1 m/s is scored as
  16: parked, so a trajectory cutting across its face is scored as safe.
  17: 
  18: This controller gives the obstacles a time axis of their own::
  19: 
  20:     diff = points[:, :, None, :] - predicted[None, :, :, :]
  21:     #      (N, K, 2)                (1,  K,  M, 2)   <- same K
  22: 
  23: **What it is not allowed to buy.** Prediction earns speed and smoothness,
  24: never safety. Both hard constraints are the ones ``dwa`` has, unchanged
  25: and measured on the same quantities:
  26: 
  27: * the **set** refusal â€” ``clearances <= hard_clearance`` â€” is computed
  28:   from the points the LiDAR returned **at this instant**, exactly as
  29:   before. Feeding it predicted clearances would let
  30:   ``prediction_horizon_seconds``, a candidate parameter, shrink the hard
  31:   feasible set the global planner planned against, which is precisely
  32:   what contract L2 forbids;
  33: * the **speed** bound â€” the admissible-stopping limit â€” is likewise
  34:   untouched, and reads the same declared ``v_obstacle_max``.
  35: 
  36: So ``dwa_predictive`` may not enter anywhere ``dwa`` is forbidden. It may
  37: only pass *sooner* through somewhere both are allowed. The argument for
  38: that is stronger than the contract: **an estimate used to relax a safety
  39: bound turns estimation error into collisions, while an estimate used in a
  40: cost turns it into a suboptimal route.** This module's velocities are
  41: estimates with three known failure modes (P5), and giving a quantity with
  42: three known failure modes the power to lower a safety threshold is
  43: choosing the wrong direction to be wrong in.
  44: 
  45: **Not a subclass of** :class:`~planbench_planning.dwa.planner.DWAPlanner`,
  46: deliberately. ``StackComponent.version`` is part of a candidate's
  47: identity, so a shared parent would let one bug fix silently change two
  48: candidates while both recorded ids stayed put. The shared code lives in
  49: :mod:`planbench_planning.common.dwa_core` as pure functions instead.
  50: 
  51: **Where the tracks come from.** With no injected provider the
  52: controller does the real thing: :class:`~planbench_planning.dwa_predictive.tracking.LidarTracker`
  53: clusters the scan and estimates velocities from it, so the candidate is
  54: ``lidar_only`` and its estimation error is its own. A provider overrides
  55: that, and exactly two things use it â€” P4's ground-truth oracle, which
  56: measures the ceiling with zero estimation error, and tests that want to
  57: state the velocities themselves.
  58: 
  59: Handing it a provider returning nothing makes every predictive term
  60: exactly zero and the commands identical to ``dwa``. That is asserted
  61: rather than hoped: "the new terms switch off cleanly" is the property
  62: every later comparison rests on, and it is also what each of the

declared, and once on the same deployment with the traffic removed,

def _instrument(tracker, tally: Tally, spec, seed: int, max_range: float):
    """Wrap this tracker instance's ``update`` to count what it saw.

    Instance-level, not a patch on ``LidarTracker`` itself: a class-wide
    patch would leak into anything else sharing the process, and these
    workers run several episodes in one.
    """
    inner = tracker.update

    def observed(observation):
        tally.frames += 1
        truth = position_at(spec, observation.time, seed) if spec is not None else None
        px, py, theta = observation.pose.x, observation.pose.y, observation.pose.theta

        in_range = False
        if truth is not None:
            distance = math.hypot(truth.x - px, truth.y - py)
            in_range = distance <= max_range + spec.radius
            if in_range:
                tally.in_range += 1
                ranges = observation.lidar_ranges
                rays = len(ranges)
                spacing = 2.0 * math.pi / rays
                start = theta - math.pi
                limit = max(ranges)
                hits = 0
                for index, reading in enumerate(ranges):
                    if reading >= limit - 1e-9:
                        continue
                    ex = px + reading * math.cos(start + index * spacing)
                    ey = py + reading * math.sin(start + index * spacing)
                    if math.hypot(ex - truth.x, ey - truth.y) <= spec.radius + RAY_HIT_MARGIN_M:
                        hits += 1
                tally.hit_rays += hits
                if hits:
                    tally.scanned += 1
                reach = spec.radius + MATCH_MARGIN_M
                near = [
                    cluster
                    for cluster in tracker.cluster(observation)
                    if math.hypot(cluster.centroid.x - truth.x, cluster.centroid.y - truth.y)
                    < reach
                ]
                if near:
                    tally.clustered += 1
                    if any(tracker._is_free_standing(cluster) for cluster in near):
                        tally.passed += 1

        tracks = inner(observation)

        if truth is not None and in_range:
            reach = spec.radius + MATCH_MARGIN_M
            for track in tracks:
                if math.hypot(track.center.x - truth.x, track.center.y - truth.y) >= reach:
                    continue
                tally.tracked += 1
                speed = math.hypot(track.velocity.x, track.velocity.y)
                if speed > 1e-9:
                    tally.velocity_reported += 1
                    ahead = position_at(spec, observation.time + TRUTH_DT, seed)
                    tvx = (ahead.x - truth.x) / TRUTH_DT
                    tvy = (ahead.y - truth.y) / TRUTH_DT
                    tally.velocity_errors.append(
                        math.hypot(track.velocity.x - tvx, track.velocity.y - tvy)
                    )
                break

        if spec is None:
            # Static scene: nothing moves, so every reported velocity is
            # a phantom by construction. No matching needed and none
            # possible — there is no true object to match against.
            speeds = [
                math.hypot(track.velocity.x, track.velocity.y)
                for track in tracks
                if math.hypot(track.velocity.x, track.velocity.y) > 1e-9
            ]
            if speeds:
                tally.phantom_frames += 1
                tally.phantom_speeds.append(max(speeds))

        return tracks

    tracker.update = observed

    context = build_evaluation_contexts(profile, seed_count=1, first_seed=seed)[0]

    )

    local_planner = build_local_planner(STACK, LOCAL_CONTROLLER_CONFIGS[CONTROLLER_CONFIG])

    tally = Tally()
    _instrument(local_planner._tracker, tally, spec, context.seed, scenario.lidar.max_range)

    started = time.perf_counter()
    run = run_stack(
        map_data,
        scenario,
        local_planner,
        global_planner,
        profile.replanning,
        recovery=profile.recovery,
        legacy_metrics=False,
        obstacle_speed=profile.environment.v_obstacle_max,

def _median(values: list[float]) -> float:
    return statistics.median(values) if values else float("nan")


def _percentile(values: list[float], fraction: float) -> float:
    if not values:
        return float("nan")
    ordered = sorted(values)
    index = min(len(ordered) - 1, int(round(fraction * (len(ordered) - 1))))
    return ordered[index]


def summarise(rows: list[dict], rays: int) -> dict:
    traffic = [row for row in rows if row["rays"] == rays and not row["static"]]
    static = [row for row in rows if row["rays"] == rays and row["static"]]

    in_range = sum(row["in_range"] for row in traffic)
    denominator = max(in_range, 1)
    errors = [value for row in traffic for value in row["velocity_errors"]]
    phantom_frames = sum(row["phantom_frames"] for row in static)
    static_frames = sum(row["frames"] for row in static)
    phantom_speeds = [value for row in static for value in row["phantom_speeds"]]

    return {
        "rays": rays,
        "degrees": 360.0 / rays,
        "episodes_traffic": len(traffic),
        "episodes_static": len(static),
        "in_range_frames": in_range,
        "scanned_frames": sum(row["scanned"] for row in traffic),

        "velocity_report_rate": sum(row["velocity_reported"] for row in traffic) / denominator,
        "velocity_error_median": _median(errors),
        "velocity_error_n": len(errors),
        "phantom_rate": phantom_frames / max(static_frames, 1),
        "phantom_speed_p90": _percentile(phantom_speeds, 0.90),

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)

        "--rays",
        type=str,

    resolutions = tuple(int(value) for value in args.rays.split(","))
    seeds = tuple(CALIBRATION_FIRST_SEED + offset for offset in range(args.seeds))
    import os

    workers = args.workers or max(1, min(8, (os.cpu_count() or 4) - 2))

    print("Q0 — LiDAR angular resolution against the tracker")
    print(f"profile      {PROFILE.name}   candidate {STACK}:{CONTROLLER_CONFIG}")
    print()
    print("seed policy (calibration and evaluation are disjoint, and stay that way):")
    for label, value in SEED_POLICY.items():
        print(f"  {value:<12} {label}")

    print("objective for choosing a configuration, fixed before the table exists:")
    for line in OBJECTIVE:
        print(f"  {line}")
    print()
    print("NOT measured here: latency. Episodes run in parallel, so a p99 from")
    print("this run would be meaningless. G4 belongs to Q5, on a pinned host.")
    print()

    jobs = [
        (rays, seed, static)
        for rays in resolutions
        for seed in seeds
        for static in (False, True)
    ]
    print(f"{len(jobs)} episodes on {workers} workers…", flush=True)

    started = time.perf_counter()
    rows: list[dict] = []
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        for done, row in enumerate(pool.map(_job, jobs), start=1):
            rows.append(row)
            if done % 10 == 0 or done == len(jobs):
                print(f"  {done}/{len(jobs)}", flush=True)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started

    summaries = [summarise(rows, rays) for rays in resolutions]

    print()
    print("scene with traffic — measured against the obstacle's true position")
    print(" rays   deg  in_range  rays/f  clustered  passed  vel_out   err_med    n")
    for row in summaries:
        print(
            f"{row['rays']:>5} {row['degrees']:5.2f} {row['in_range_frames']:>9}"
            f" {row['rays_per_frame']:7.2f} {100 * row['clustered_rate']:9.1f}%"
            f" {100 * row['passed_rate']:6.1f}% {100 * row['velocity_report_rate']:7.1f}%"
            f" {row['velocity_error_median']:9.3f} {row['velocity_error_n']:>4}"
        )

    print()
    print("static scene — same deployment, traffic removed; every velocity is a phantom")
    print(" rays   phantom_rate   phantom_p90")
    for row in summaries:
        print(f"{row['rays']:>5} {100 * row['phantom_rate']:13.2f}% {row['phantom_speed_p90']:13.3f}")

    baseline = next((row for row in summaries if row["rays"] == 72), None)
    print()
    print("objective applied:")
    if baseline is None:
        print("  no 72-ray baseline in this run — hard constraint cannot be evaluated")
    else:
        eligible = [
            row for row in summaries if row["phantom_rate"] <= baseline["phantom_rate"] + 1e-12
        ]
        for row in summaries:
            verdict = "eligible" if row in eligible else "REJECTED by hard constraint"
            print(
                f"  {row['rays']:>4} rays  phantom {100 * row['phantom_rate']:6.2f}%"
                f"  vs baseline {100 * baseline['phantom_rate']:6.2f}%   {verdict}"
            )
        if eligible:
            best = max(eligible, key=lambda row: row["velocity_report_rate"])
            print(
                f"  -> maximum velocity_report_rate among eligible: {best['rays']} rays"
                f" at {100 * best['velocity_report_rate']:.1f}%"
            )
        else:
            print("  -> no configuration satisfies the hard constraint")

    print()
    print(f"wall clock {elapsed / 60:.1f} min across {workers} workers")

    if args.out:
        args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        args.out.write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "profile": PROFILE.name,
                    "stack": STACK,
                    "controller_config": CONTROLLER_CONFIG,
                    "seed_policy": SEED_POLICY,
                    "seeds": list(seeds),
                    "objective": list(OBJECTIVE),
                    "summaries": summaries,
                    "rows": rows,
                },
                indent=1,
            ),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        print(f"raw rows -> {args.out}")

    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

    log_path = args.out.with_suffix(".jsonl") if args.out else None
    done_keys: set[tuple[int, int, bool]] = set()

---

## 0. Q0 tồn tại để làm gì, và nó đã làm đúng việc đó

Plan 16-08 được dựng trên một bảng đo **một seed**, trung vị lấy trên
2–17 frame. Q0 là pha chạy lại ở N ≥ 20 trước khi sửa bất cứ thứ gì, và
plan đã ghi sẵn rủi ro của nó:

> Q0 có thể huỷ toàn bộ phần còn lại. Đó là mục đích của nó.

Nó đã huỷ. Hai phát hiện dưới đây, cái thứ nhất bác bỏ bảng cũ, cái thứ
hai bác bỏ hướng đi của cả plan.

---

## 1. Thiết lập

| | |
|---|---|
| Deployment | `warehouse_crossing_v1`, AMR cắt ngang 0.8 m/s hằng số |
| Candidate | `astar+dwa_predictive : dwa_predictive_balanced` |

Nhánh tĩnh là bắt buộc chứ không phải phụ: chỉ đo cảnh có traffic thì
**mọi** thay đổi làm tracker nhạy hơn đều trông như cải thiện. Trên cảnh
tĩnh, theo định nghĩa, mọi vận tốc báo ra đều là ảo.

  144  2.50    17/20      2403    3.55      33.1%    4.6%     3.5%     0.935   84

## 3. Phát hiện 1 — bảng một-seed của plan **bị bác bỏ**

Bảng §1.4 của plan nói: đỉnh ở 144 tia, **thoái lui** ở 271 và 360.

---
name: plan
description: Strategic planning with optional interview workflow
---

<Purpose>
Plan creates comprehensive, actionable work plans through intelligent interaction. It auto-detects whether to interview the user (broad requests) or plan directly (detailed requests), and supports consensus mode (iterative Planner/Architect/Critic loop with RALPLAN-DR structured deliberation) and review mode (Critic evaluation of existing plans).
</Purpose>

<Use_When>
- User wants to plan before implementing -- "plan this", "plan the", "let's plan"
- User wants structured requirements gathering for a vague idea
- User wants an existing plan reviewed -- "review this plan", `--review`
- User wants multi-perspective consensus on a plan -- `--consensus`, "ralplan"
- Task is broad or vague and needs scoping before any code is written
</Use_When>

<Do_Not_Use_When>
- User wants autonomous end-to-end execution -- use `autopilot` instead
- User wants to start coding immediately with a clear task -- use `ralph` or delegate to executor
- User asks a simple question that can be answered directly -- just answer it
- Task is a single focused fix with obvious scope -- skip planning, just do it
</Do_Not_Use_When>

<Why_This_Exists>
Jumping into code without understanding requirements leads to rework, scope creep, and missed edge cases. Plan provides structured requirements gathering, expert analysis, and quality-gated plans so that execution starts from a solid foundation. The consensus mode adds multi-perspective validation for high-stakes projects.
</Why_This_Exists>

<Execution_Policy>
- Auto-detect interview vs direct mode based on request specificity
- Ask one question at a time during interviews -- never batch multiple questions
- Gather codebase facts via `explore` agent before asking the user about them
- When session guidance enables `USE_OMX_EXPLORE_CMD`, prefer `omx explore` for simple read-only repository lookups during planning; keep prompts narrow and concrete, and keep prompt-heavy or ambiguous planning work on the richer normal path and fall back normally if `omx explore` is unavailable.
- Plans must meet quality standards: 80%+ claims cite file/line, 90%+ criteria are testable
- Implementation step count must be right-sized to task scope; avoid defaulting to exactly five steps when the work is clearly smaller or larger
- Consensus mode outputs the final plan by default; add `--interactive` to enable execution handoff
- Consensus mode uses RALPLAN-DR short mode by default; switch to deliberate mode with `--deliberate` or when the request explicitly signals high risk (auth/security, data migration, destructive/irreversible changes, production incident, compliance/PII, public API breakage)
- Default to concise, evidence-dense progress and completion reporting unless the user or risk level requires more detail
- Treat newer user task updates as local overrides for the active workflow branch while preserving earlier non-conflicting constraints
- If correctness depends on additional inspection, retrieval, execution, or verification, keep using the relevant tools until the plan is grounded
- Continue through clear, low-risk, reversible next steps automatically; ask only when the next step is materially branching, destructive, or preference-dependent
</Execution_Policy>

<Steps>

### Mode Selection

| Mode | Trigger | Behavior |
|------|---------|----------|
| Interview | Default for broad requests | Interactive requirements gathering |
| Direct | `--direct`, or detailed request | Skip interview, generate plan directly |
| Consensus | `--consensus`, "ralplan" | Planner -> Architect -> Critic loop until agreement with RALPLAN-DR structured deliberation (short by default, `--deliberate` for high-risk); outputs plan by default |
| Consensus Interactive | `--consensus --interactive` | Same as Consensus but pauses for user feedback at draft and approval steps, then hands off to execution |
| Review | `--review`, "review this plan" | Critic evaluation of existing plan |

### Interview Mode (broad/vague requests)

1. **Classify the request**: Broad (vague verbs, no specific files, touches 3+ areas) triggers interview mode
2. **Ask one focused question** using `AskUserQuestion` for preferences, scope, and constraints
3. **Gather codebase facts first**: Before asking "what patterns does your code use?", spawn an `explore` agent to find out, then ask informed follow-up questions
4. **Build on answers**: Each question builds on the previous answer
5. **Consult Analyst** (THOROUGH tier) for hidden requirements, edge cases, and risks
6. **Create plan** when the user signals readiness: "create the plan", "I'm ready", "make it a work plan"

### Direct Mode (detailed requests)

1. **Quick Analysis**: Optional brief Analyst consultation
2. **Create plan**: Generate comprehensive work plan immediately
3. **Review** (optional): Critic review if requested

### Consensus Mode (`--consensus` / "ralplan")

**RALPLAN-DR modes**: **Short** (default, bounded structure) and **Deliberate** (for `--deliberate` or explicit high-risk requests). Both modes keep the same Planner -> Architect -> Critic sequence. The workflow auto-proceeds through planning steps (Planner/Architect/Critic) but outputs the final plan without executing.

1. **Planner** creates initial plan and a compact **RALPLAN-DR summary** before any Architect review. The summary **MUST** include:
   - **Principles** (3-5)
   - **Decision Drivers** (top 3)
   - **Viable Options** (>=2) with bounded pros/cons for each option
   - If only one viable option remains, an explicit **invalidation rationale** for the alternatives that were rejected
   - In **deliberate mode**: a **pre-mortem** (3 failure scenarios) and an **expanded test plan** covering **unit / integration / e2e / observability**
2. **User feedback** *(--interactive only)*: If running with `--interactive`, **MUST** use `AskUserQuestion` to present the draft plan **plus the RALPLAN-DR Principles / Decision Drivers / Options summary for early direction alignment** with these options:
   - **Proceed to review** — send to Architect and Critic for evaluation
   - **Request changes** — return to step 1 with user feedback incorporated
   - **Skip review** — go directly to final approval (step 7)
   If NOT running with `--interactive`, automatically proceed to review (step 3).
3. **Architect** reviews for architectural soundness using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "architect"`. Architect review **MUST** include: strongest steelman counterargument (antithesis) against the favored option, at least one meaningful tradeoff tension, and (when possible) a synthesis path. In deliberate mode, Architect should explicitly flag principle violations. **Wait for this step to complete before proceeding to step 4.** Do NOT run steps 3 and 4 in parallel.
4. **Critic** evaluates against quality criteria using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "critic"`. Critic **MUST** verify principle-option consistency, fair alternative exploration, risk mitigation clarity, testable acceptance criteria, and concrete verification steps. Critic **MUST** explicitly reject shallow alternatives, driver contradictions, vague risks, or weak verification. In deliberate mode, Critic **MUST** reject missing/weak pre-mortem or missing/weak expanded test plan. Run only after step 3 is complete.
5. **Re-review loop** (max 5 iterations): If Critic rejects or iterates, execute this closed loop:
   a. Collect all feedback from Architect + Critic
   b. Pass feedback to Planner to produce a revised plan
   c. **Return to Step 3** — Architect reviews the revised plan
   d. **Return to Step 4** — Critic evaluates the revised plan
   e. Repeat until Critic approves OR max 5 iterations reached
   f. If max iterations reached without approval, present the best version to user via `AskUserQuestion` with note that expert consensus was not reached
6. **Apply improvements**: When reviewers approve with improvement suggestions, merge all accepted improvements into the plan file before proceeding. Final consensus output **MUST** include an **ADR** section with: **Decision**, **Drivers**, **Alternatives considered**, **Why chosen**, **Consequences**, **Follow-ups**. Specifically:
   a. Collect all improvement suggestions from Architect and Critic responses
   b. Deduplicate and categorize the suggestions
   c. Update the plan file in `.omx/plans/` with the accepted improvements (add missing details, refine steps, strengthen acceptance criteria, ADR updates, etc.)
   d. Note which improvements were applied in a brief changelog section at the end of the plan
   e. Before any execution handoff, derive an explicit **available-agent-types roster** from the known prompt catalog and add concrete **follow-up staffing guidance** for both `$ralph` and `$team` (recommended roles, counts, suggested reasoning levels by lane, and why each lane exists)
   f. For the `$team` path, add an explicit launch-hint block with concrete `omx team` / `$team` commands and a **team verification path** (what team proves before shutdown, what Ralph verifies after handoff)
7. On Critic approval (with improvements applied): *(--interactive only)* If running with `--interactive`, use `AskUserQuestion` to present the plan with these options:
   - **Approve and execute** — proceed to implementation via ralph+ultrawork
   - **Approve and implement via team** — proceed to implementation via coordinated parallel team agents
   - **Request changes** — return to step 1 with user feedback
   - **Reject** — discard the plan entirely
   If NOT running with `--interactive`, output the final approved plan and stop. Do NOT auto-execute.
8. *(--interactive only)* User chooses via the structured `AskUserQuestion` UI (never ask for approval in plain text)
9. On user approval (--interactive only):
   - **Approve and execute**: **MUST** invoke `$ralph` with the approved plan path from `.omx/plans/` as context **plus the explicit available-agent-types roster, suggested reasoning levels, concrete role allocation guidance, and direct launch hints for Ralph follow-up work**. Do NOT implement directly. Do NOT edit source code files in the planning agent. The ralph skill handles execution via ultrawork parallel agents.
   - **Approve and implement via team**: **MUST** invoke `$team` with the approved plan path from `.omx/plans/` as context **plus the explicit available-agent-types roster, suggested reasoning levels, concrete staffing / worker-role allocation guidance, explicit `omx team` / `$team` launch hints, and the team verification path**. Do NOT implement directly. The team skill coordinates parallel agents across the staged pipeline for faster execution on large tasks.

### Review Mode (`--review`)

0. Treat review as a reviewer-only pass. The context that wrote the plan, cleanup proposal, or diff MUST NOT be the context that approves it.
1. Read plan file from `.omx/plans/`
2. Evaluate via Critic using `ask_codex` with `agent_role: "critic"`
3. For cleanup/refactor/anti-slop work, verify that the artifact includes a cleanup plan, regression tests or an explicit test gap, smell-by-smell passes, and quality gates.
4. Return verdict: APPROVED, REVISE (with specific feedback), or REJECT (replanning required)
5. If the current context authored the artifact, hand the review to `/review`, `critic`, `quality-reviewer`, `security-reviewer`, or `verifier` as appropriate.

### Plan Output Format

Every plan includes:
- Requirements Summary
- Acceptance Criteria (testable)
- Implementation Steps (with file references)
- Adaptive step count sized to the actual scope (not a fixed five-step template)
- Risks and Mitigations
- Verification Steps
- For consensus/ralplan: **RALPLAN-DR summary** (Principles, Decision Drivers, Options)
- For consensus/ralplan final output: **ADR** (Decision, Drivers, Alternatives considered, Why chosen, Consequences, Follow-ups)
- For consensus/ralplan execution handoff: **Available-Agent-Types Roster**, **Follow-up Staffing Guidance** (including suggested reasoning levels by lane), explicit `omx team` / `$team` **Launch Hints**, and **Team Verification Path**

Plans are saved to `.omx/plans/`. Drafts go to `.omx/drafts/`.

**Good:** The user says `continue` after the workflow already has a clear next step. Continue the current branch of work instead of restarting or re-asking the same question.

**Good:** The user changes only the output shape or downstream delivery step (for example `make a PR`). Preserve earlier non-conflicting workflow constraints and apply the update locally.

Planner: [receives: "Auth is in src/auth/ using JWT with passport.js"]

  73: Ở N = 20 **không có thoái lui nào**. `vel_out` tăng đơn điệu:
  74: 
  75: | | một seed | N = 20 |
  76: |---|---|---|
  77: | 72 | 1.4% | 0.9% |
  78: | 144 | **11.8%** | 3.5% |
  79: | 271 | 9.0% | 4.1% |
  80: | 360 | 8.7% | 4.5% |

  82: 
  83: Con số `0.164 m/s` từng là bằng chứng mạnh nhất cho "144 tia là điểm
  84: ngọt" — ở N = 20 nó là **0.935 m/s**, tức sai số cỡ chính tốc độ cần đo.

  95: ## 4. Phát hiện 2 — cái giá thật của độ phân giải
  96: 
  97: Đi từ 72 lên 360 tia:
  98: 
  99: ```
 100: phát hiện thật:  0.9%  ->  4.5%     ( x5 )
 101: ảo giác:        14.2%  -> 99.2%     ( x7 )
 102: ```
 103: 
 104: Ở 360 tia, trong một nhà kho **không có gì chuyển động**, tracker báo có
 105: vật đang di chuyển ở **99.19% số frame**. p90 tốc độ ảo 2.02 m/s — gấp
 106: 2.5 lần traffic thật.

 109: 
 110: ```
 111: ràng buộc cứng: phantom_rate <= baseline 72 tia (14.17%)
 112:   144 tia  78.56%  TRƯỢT
 113:   271 tia  97.52%  TRƯỢT
 114:   360 tia  99.19%  TRƯỢT
 115: => cấu hình hợp lệ duy nhất: 72 tia — chính cái đang chạy
 116: ```
 117: 
 118: ---
 119: 
 120: ## 5. Cơ chế — sàn vận tốc mô hình sai đại lượng
 121: 
 122: Câu hỏi tôi tự đặt trước khi có số: mức tăng ảo là do **nhiều track hơn**
 123: hay **mỗi track tệ hơn**? Đo riêng để trả lời, và đáp án là **cả hai**:
 124: 
 125: ```
 126: tracks/frame:   4.32  -> 25.72     ( x6.0 )
 127: per-track ảo:  3.54%  -> 22.88%    ( x6.5 )
 128: ```
 129: 
 130: Hai thừa số nhân nhau ra 14% → 99%.
 131: 
 132: Vế thứ hai mới là vế quan trọng, vì nó nói **giảm số track rác là không
 133: đủ**. Bằng chứng nằm ở một cột trông có vẻ tầm thường:
 134: 
 135: ```
 136: phantom_p90:  1.868   1.515   1.820   2.023      <- gần như PHẲNG
 137: ```
 138: 
 139: Biên độ vận tốc ảo **không đổi** theo độ phân giải. Trong khi đó sàn
 140: chặn nó co lại tuyến tính:
 141: 
 142: ```
 143: velocity_floor = (2·σ_pose + margin·σ_range + reach·Δθ) / window
 144:                                               ^^^^^^^^^
 145: tại 4 m:  72 tia -> 0.584 m/s        360 tia -> 0.186 m/s
 146: ```
 147: 
 148: Số hạng `reach·Δθ` — thứ tôi thêm vào ở P5 để mô hình hoá lượng tử hoá
 149: tia — đang gánh gần như toàn bộ việc chặn ảo ở 72 tia. Nó giả định
 150: **biên độ ảo tỉ lệ với khoảng cách tia**. Phép đo nói biên độ ảo
 151: **không phụ thuộc khoảng cách tia**.
 152: 
 153: Nghĩa là sàn đúng ở 72 tia vì **trùng hợp về độ lớn**, không phải vì mô
 154: hình đúng. Nguồn ảo trội thực sự là centroid trượt dọc bề mặt khi robot
 155: di chuyển — phụ thuộc chuyển động của robot, không phụ thuộc Δθ.
 156:

 160: 
 161: Tiền đề trung tâm của plan 16-08 là:
 162: 
 163: > tăng độ phân giải là đòn bẩy chính; Q1 làm cảm biến khai được, Q2 làm
 164: > ngưỡng co giãn theo cảm biến để việc tăng tia thôi phản tác dụng.
 165: 
 166: Tiền đề này **không đứng vững**. Q1 + Q2 như đang viết sẽ mở đường cho
 167: một cấu hình mà tracker ảo giác gần như mọi frame.

 169: Và Q2b (test tường theo tính liên tục) — pha tôi đặt nhiều kỳ vọng nhất
 170: — chỉ tấn công thừa số `tracks/frame`. Kể cả nếu nó hoàn hảo, đưa
 171: 25.72 track/frame về 4.32, thì `per-track` vẫn 22.88% thay vì 3.54%, và
 172: phantom_rate ở 360 tia vẫn cao hơn baseline nhiều lần.
 173: 
 174: **Thứ tự đúng đảo lại:** sàn vận tốc phải được thiết kế lại **trước**,
 175: dựa trên một mô hình biên độ ảo khớp với phép đo (phẳng theo Δθ, phụ
 176: thuộc chuyển động robot). Mọi việc về độ phân giải chỉ có nghĩa sau đó.
 177: 
 178: Đề xuất cụ thể để dev chốt: xem mục "Đề xuất sửa plan" trong phần cập
 179: nhật của `plans/2026-08-16/sua-tri-giac-dwa-predictive.md`.

 183: ## 7. Ba thứ về phương pháp, lộ ra khi dựng harness
 184: 
 185: **(a) Bản đo đầu tiên là bản đo hư, và nó im lặng.**

 187: còn `run_stack` gọi `reset` sau khi caller kịp bọc instance. Wrapper bị
 188: vứt trước scan đầu tiên ⇒ episode chạy **thành công**, mọi counter bằng
 189: 0, bảng đọc ra "tracker không thấy gì" thay vì "không ai đang đo".

 196: 
 197: **(c) Ghim BLAS về 1 luồng là đòn bẩy tốc độ, không phải chi tiết.**

 199: numpy giành đúng số core mà script muốn dùng cho episode. Ghim xong:
 200: 160 episode trong 27.6 phút. Ghi trong script kèm số đo, vì nó là điều

 205: tracker sẽ **từ chối** dòng cũ thay vì trộn hai phiên bản vào một bảng.

+### Q0-KQ.2 — Cơ chế, và vì sao Q2 không giải được
+
+Ảo tăng do **cả hai** thừa số: `tracks/frame` ×6.0 **và** `per-track`
+×6.5. Q2b (test tường) chỉ tấn công thừa số thứ nhất. Kể cả nếu nó hoàn
+hảo — đưa 25.72 track/frame về 4.32 — thì `per-track` vẫn 22.88% thay
+vì 3.54%, và ảo vẫn cao hơn baseline nhiều lần.
+
+Bằng chứng quyết định nằm ở cột `p90`: biên độ vận tốc ảo **phẳng**
+(1.5–2.0 m/s) qua mọi độ phân giải, trong khi sàn chặn nó co tuyến tính
+theo `Δθ`:
+
+```
+velocity_floor = (2·σ_pose + margin·σ_range + reach·Δθ) / window
+tại 4 m:  72 tia -> 0.584 m/s      360 tia -> 0.186 m/s
+```
+
+Số hạng `reach·Δθ` (thêm ở P5) giả định **biên độ ảo tỉ lệ khoảng cách
+tia**. Phép đo nói **không**. Sàn đúng ở 72 tia vì trùng hợp độ lớn,
+không vì mô hình đúng. Nguồn ảo trội thật sự là centroid trượt dọc bề
+mặt khi robot di chuyển — phụ thuộc chuyển động robot, không phụ thuộc
+`Δθ`.
+
+### Q0-KQ.3 — Đề xuất sửa hướng
+

+phân giải.** Plan mới đề xuất:
+
+| pha | việc | vì sao trước |
+|---|---|---|
+| **R1** | Đo nguồn ảo trội: tách đóng góp của (i) lượng tử hoá tia, (ii) centroid trượt theo chuyển động robot, (iii) nhiễu range. Cảnh tĩnh, robot **đứng yên** vs **di chuyển** | `p90` phẳng nói mô hình hiện tại sai; phải biết sai ở đâu trước khi viết công thức mới |
+| **R2** | Thiết kế lại sàn từ mô hình đo được ở R1. Nhiều khả năng có số hạng tỉ lệ **tốc độ robot**, không tỉ lệ `Δθ` | Đây là thứ chặn ảo; sửa nó là điều kiện cần cho mọi việc sau |

+Q1 (cảm biến deployment-owned) **vẫn có giá trị độc lập** — nó là điều
+kiện để so hai cảm biến ở bất kỳ phép đo nào, kể cả R3, và nó đi kèm

+
+Q2a/Q2b/Q2c chuyển thành **có điều kiện**: chỉ có nghĩa sau khi R2 xong
+và R3 cho thấy độ phân giải cao trở nên dùng được.
+
+### Q0-KQ.4 — Khả năng phải chấp nhận
+
+Nếu R1 cho thấy nguồn ảo trội là centroid trượt dọc tường theo chuyển
+động robot, thì đó **không phải** thứ một cái sàn vô hướng chặn được —
+nó cần phân biệt "cụm này là bề mặt tĩnh" với "cụm này là vật", tức
+đúng bài toán mà `_is_free_standing` đang giải sai. Khi đó câu trả lời
+trung thực có thể là: **tri giác 2D LiDAR đơn thuần không đủ để ước
+lượng vận tốc vật cản trong môi trường có tường gần**, và
+`dwa_predictive` nên đóng bằng kết quả âm theo nhánh (c) của §Q4.
+
+Ghi trước ở đây để nhánh đó không bị coi là thất bại của người thực hiện
+khi nó xảy ra.
